If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 5 days, reduce forecasted decline in early horizon (1–7 days) by 5–10% to avoid over-selling.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 5 days, increase forecasted rise in mid horizon (8–15 days) by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.

When sentiment swings from positive to negative within 3 days, shift forecast peak earlier (by 1–3 days) and reduce late horizon (16–30) by 10–15% to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.33) across 7+ days, apply linear smoothing to forecast path, reducing volatility in mid horizon by 20–30% to avoid overreaction.

If sentiment is positive but recent price is falling, add a 3–5 day lagged correction to forecast, reducing slope downward by 10–15% to prevent premature sell-off.

If sentiment is negative but recent price is rising, apply a 3–5 day lagged correction to forecast, increasing slope upward by 10–15% to prevent false optimism.
